title: What Is Flexbox?
body:
CSS Flexbox is a one-dimensional layout module designed to arrange items within a container along a single axis. It provides an efficient way to distribute space among items and align them, making complex responsive designs much simpler to implement.

It's particularly useful for small-scale layouts, component alignment, and distributing space evenly. Flexbox helps in creating dynamic interfaces that adapt well to different screen sizes without complex calculations.

title: Container And Items
body:
In Flexbox, there are two primary entities: the flex container and flex items. The flex container is the parent element on which `display: flex` or `display: inline-flex` is applied. It dictates how its direct children, known as flex items, are laid out.

Flex items are the direct children of a flex container. They automatically become flex items when their parent is a flex container and gain the ability to be manipulated by flexbox properties. All flexbox properties either apply to the container or to the items.

title: Main And Cross Axes
body:
Flexbox operates along two axes: the main axis and the cross axis. The main axis is defined by `flex-direction` and can be horizontal (row) or vertical (column). Items are laid out along this axis.

The cross axis is perpendicular to the main axis. If the main axis is horizontal, the cross axis is vertical, and vice versa. Understanding these axes is crucial for correctly aligning and justifying items within your flex container.

title: Direction And Wrapping
body:
`flex-direction` sets the primary axis along which flex items are laid out, determining if they are arranged in a row or column, and in what direction. Options include `row`, `row-reverse`, `column`, and `column-reverse`.

`flex-wrap` controls whether flex items are forced onto a single line or can wrap onto multiple lines. `nowrap` (default) keeps items on one line, `wrap` allows wrapping, and `wrap-reverse` wraps in the opposite direction. `flex-flow` is a shorthand for `flex-direction` and `flex-wrap`.

title: Justify Content
body:
`justify-content` aligns flex items along the main axis of the flex container. It distributes extra space when items don't fill the entire container or when they overflow. This property is applied to the flex container.

Common values include `flex-start` (default), `flex-end`, `center`, `space-between` (distributes space evenly between items), `space-around` (distributes space around items), and `space-evenly` (distributes space evenly around and between items).

title: Align Items And Content
body:
`align-items` aligns flex items along the cross axis when they are on a single line. It's applied to the flex container and controls how items are positioned perpendicular to the main axis. Values include `flex-start`, `flex-end`, `center`, `baseline`, and `stretch` (default).

`align-content` aligns a flex container's lines within the container when there is extra space in the cross-axis. This property only applies when `flex-wrap` is set to `wrap` or `wrap-reverse` and there are multiple lines of items. Values are similar to `justify-content`.

title: Item Order
body:
The `order` property controls the visual order of flex items within their flex container, irrespective of their source order in the HTML. By default, all flex items have an `order` value of `0`. Items with lower `order` values appear before items with higher values.

If multiple items have the same `order` value, their original source order is maintained among them. This property is particularly useful for reordering content for different screen sizes or accessibility without altering the DOM structure.

title: Growth, Shrinkage, Basis
body:
`flex-grow` defines the ability for a flex item to grow if necessary. It takes a unitless value that serves as a proportion. If all items have `flex-grow: 1`, they will consume available space equally. A value of `0` (default) prevents growth.

`flex-shrink` defines the ability for a flex item to shrink if necessary. It also takes a unitless value. A value of `1` (default) allows shrinking, while `0` prevents it. `flex-basis` sets the initial main size of a flex item before any available space is distributed; it can be a length (e.g., `200px`) or a keyword like `auto` (default).

description: This example shows how `flex-grow`, `flex-shrink`, and `flex-basis` control how individual flex items grow, shrink, and their initial size.

title: Flex Shorthand, Align Self
body:
`flex` is a shorthand property for `flex-grow`, `flex-shrink`, and `flex-basis` combined. Common values include `flex: 1` (equivalent to `1 1 0%`), `flex: auto` (equivalent to `1 1 auto`), and `flex: none` (equivalent to `0 0 auto`). Using the shorthand is generally recommended for brevity and consistency.

`align-self` allows individual flex items to override the default alignment set by `align-items` on the flex container. It accepts the same values as `align-items`: `auto` (default), `flex-start`, `flex-end`, `center`, `baseline`, and `stretch`. This provides fine-grained control over item alignment on the cross axis.
